name: fast-sqrt-one-ulp-below-the-correctly-rounded-root
rationale:
out[i] = sqrt(in[3i]^2 + in[3i+1]^2), one float per thread, 64 threads all given the same pair. The second component is exactly zero, so the sum is exactly fl(a*a) whether the multiply-add contracts or not, and the only thing left in the answer is which square root ran.

a is 0x4033ac58 (2.807394027709961) and fl(a*a) is 7.881461. At that argument Metal's fast::sqrt returns 0x4033ac59 and precise::sqrt returns 0x4033ac58 -- one ULP apart. AIR names air.fast_sqrt.f32, so the Metal oracle computes the fast root, and the case is an exact comparison against those bytes.

That one ULP is the point. SPIRV-Cross renders GLSL Sqrt as the UNQUALIFIED MSL sqrt, so which root a Vulkan consumer runs is decided entirely by the fast-math setting its runtime compiler uses, which nothing in this repository configures. Device-measured on apple-m3-max over 20000 arguments: fast::sqrt and precise::sqrt disagree on 4126 of them, and the unqualified spelling equals fast:: on all 20000 under the Metal front end's defaults. This case is the standing evidence that MoltenVK's default resolves the same way -- it Matches at MoltenVK's default and with MVK_CONFIG_FAST_MATH_ENABLED=1, and Mismatches with =0. Roughly 2000 corpus sources name a fast-spelled float transcendental that reaches an unqualified MSL name; this is the one case that would notice if that stopped being true.

The case is deliberately one ULP wide, so it is environment-specific by construction. That is what the per-environment candidate slot is for: the claim is about apple-m3-max, and a device whose fast root differs is a different observation, not a failure of this case.

name: cross-library-geometry-modifier-zero-constants
rationale: Three finite float3 positions exercise the vertex entry with every unconditional input present and all optional function-constant resources disabled. Zeroed constant structures keep all indexed accesses in bounds. The exact cross-library geometryModifierUIWithCustomParams module updates UV1 through its recursively closed API helpers; the position observer captures all three emitted clip-space positions byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-one-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 21 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-three-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: widen-a-byte-row-stride-into-a-ushort-texture-with-the-first-two-channels-swapped
rationale: The source addresses its `uchar4` buffer by raw bytes -- the first getelementptr walks a `<4 x i8>` with a leading zero index, so `JabBytesPerRow * blockcoord.y` is a byte cursor, and only the second one advances in whole uchar4 steps. This case sets the row stride to 20 bytes while dispatching only 4 columns, so each row's fifth uchar4 is never read: a translation that recovered the stride as width*4 = 16 instead of the buffer's 20 would pull those spare bytes in from row 1 onward and say so. Buffer byte `o` holds `4*o + 3`, which is injective over the whole 60-byte window and puts every byte from offset 32 upward above 127, so the zero-extension to ushort is separated from a sign-extension: 0xDF must widen to 223, not 65503. The four loaded bytes are written with the first two channels swapped, which is what fixes the component order. The destination texture is 5x4 while the grid is 4x3, so its last column and last row keep their 0xCC poison and pin the write coordinate.

name: vertex-id-fullscreen-position-single-amplification
rationale: Vertex IDs 0, 1, and 2 generate the oversized full-screen triangle (-1,1), (3,1), and (-1,-3), each with z=w=1. The single-view draw makes amplification_id exactly zero; the typed position observer records all four covered pixels without authored vertex inputs.

name: copy-twelve-bytes-through-a-four-byte-element-pointer
rationale: Two llvm.memcpy calls of twelve bytes each whose pointers name a SINGLE float: the element-zero pointer of a [3 x float] local on one side and of a Blob's float[3] member on the other. The emitter derived the pointee, saw len >= sizeof(pointee), and emitted one OpCopyMemory per call -- four bytes where the source asks for twelve, no diagnostic, valid SPIR-V out the other end. emit_element_run_memcpy walks the run instead: six OpCopyMemory, three per direction. Buffer 0 holds two Blobs, each a uint tag and three floats. Blob 0 is tag 7 with (1, 2, 4); Blob 1 is tag 9 with the decoys (100, 200, 400). The kernel copies Blob 0's payload into a stack scratch and back out into Blob 1's, so the answer keeps Blob 0 and both tags and replaces only Blob 1's payload with (1, 2, 4). A short copy leaves 200 and 400 in place; a copy that runs off the end overwrites a tag; an off-by-one element start shifts the sequence, which three distinct exact binary32 values make visible. The AIR is hand-written because the corpus hosts are rwppHomographySolverUsingInliers at 2116 lines and the vfx_irradiance_cache pair, whose copies go through unmodelled pointer placeholders and cannot be observed at all. The payload is float rather than uchar because a uchar element run needs 8-bit storage-buffer access, which the MoltenVK pipeline in this harness refuses to create.

name: single-thread-invert-word
rationale: A single invocation reads and bitwise-inverts one explicitly initialized in/out word.

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults
rationale: Function constant 132 enables manual vertex fetch. Each of the fifteen VertexArgumentBuffer records is zero-initialized, so every embedded vertex-buffer pointer is null; the AIR helper branches around every visible-table lookup and supplies its defined default attribute. Slot zero carries the exact same-library invalid-format callback solely to give the table its structurally required float4(device uchar*) type; no callback is reachable. The only AIR loop exits when its unsigned 16-bit counter reaches 32. Zero instance/view constants produce a degenerate position, so the poisoned observation target remains deterministic. Buffer 30 and its reflected offset-zero device buffer are now authored explicitly; the invalid-format callback deterministically supplies the same default attribute when that first record is reached. This indexed AIR identity has the same reflected entry/resource/linkage contract and is authored independently.

name: constant-half4-black
rationale: The fragment entry ignores its position and viewport-index inputs and returns literal half4 (0,0,0,1) at color location zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned pixel.

name: walk-the-texel-box-a-short2-corner-pair-marks-out
rationale: mxiProcessOneQuad takes the quad's three UV corners, scales them by the colour texture's size, floors, and turns the pair into short2 with air.convert.s.v2i16.f.v2f32. That short2 is the whole geometry of the kernel: its low corner is the texel the two nested loops start reading at, and its difference against the high corner is how many times each loop runs. The case observes debugOutputTexture, which the kernel writes exactly once per visited texel, so a low corner one texel off writes a different 12 of the 64 destination texels and a wrong extent writes a different count of them; the 52 texels outside the box keep their initial bytes and assert that on their own. The corner UVs are 5/16, 7/16, 11/16 and 1/2 against a size of 8, so the products are 2.5, 3.5, 5.5 and 4.0 -- every one of them half a texel away from an integer, which is the largest margin the floor can be given -- and the resulting box is x from 2 to 5 and y from 3 to 5. It is deliberately not square, so a conversion that swapped the two lanes would start at (3, 2) and run 3 by 4 instead of 4 by 3. Each visited texel's blue lane is the alpha the kernel read there, and the twelve alphas are 0, 1/2 and 1, so the written region also reports which texels it landed on; the surrounding texels of the slice hold 3/4 and the other array slice holds 1/4, so shifting the box or reading slice 0 instead of the slice triangleSliceIndices names both change the observed image. The red lane varies texel by texel through the four corner-distance comparisons the kernel makes in half precision -- seven of the twelve texels set it and five do not. Every value is exact: the distances are square roots of integers no larger than 13 truncated back to an integer, so only the perfect squares land on the boundary and those are exact in half, and 0, 1/2, 1 and 3/4 are all exact in half.

name: and-a-broadcast-source-through-a-nullable-pointer-merge
rationale:
The nullable pointer merge is the case. `sourceB` is compared against null, and the branch that computes its element pointer feeds an OpPhi at the join whose other arm is the null; the byte is then loaded through that phi in a LATER block, on the `op != 2` arm. The arm's definition block does not dominate that load -- the join has two predecessors -- so substituting the arm for the merge at the load, which `expose_nullable_memory_bases` did unconditionally, leaves the operand undefined on the other incoming path and hands the relooper a module that is not in SSA form. This source is where that was bisected: it is one of the 11 whose bytes the dominance guard changes, and one of the 10 whose transform output violated SSA before it.

op is 0, logical AND, which is the arm that actually loads `sourceB`; op 2 is the only arm that skips the load, and every other arm reaches it. The three tensors broadcast DIFFERENTLY, which is what makes a confused pointer or a confused dims[] index visible: `get_buffer_ptr` clamps each index with smin(extent-1, index), and dims[1] (sourceB) declares its outermost extent as 1 while dims[0] and dims[2] declare 2. So sourceA and the result are indexed i + 2j + 4k + 8l over sixteen elements, and sourceB is indexed i + 2j + 4k over eight, broadcast across l. Reading B at the 16-element stride instead, or reading A where B belongs, changes the answer in half the lanes.

The two inner indices come from `decompose_global_id`, which is authored onto its shift path: IntegerDivisionParams is divisor 2, shift 1, so k = z >> 1 and l = z - 2*k = z & 1. With the grid 2x2x4 that makes (i, j, k, l) enumerate all sixteen combinations exactly once, so every result byte is written by exactly one invocation and none is written twice. The three guards ahead of the work all read dims[2] -- x against member 3, y against member 2, k against member 1, each authored 2 -- so no invocation returns early; authoring any of them as 1 would silently halve the written set.

sourceA is 1 except where t is a multiple of 3 and sourceB alternates, so the AND is 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0 -- neither operand's pattern on its own, and not the constant either operand would give if the other were dropped. The result buffer is thirty-two bytes and only the first sixteen may be written; the rest hold 0xEE, which is not a value the store can produce because it ends in `& 1`, so a stray write names the byte it hit.

name: linked-zero-destination-stencil
rationale: The authored destination extent is zero in every dimension. The sole invocation fails the combined entry bounds check before pooling/stencil loop construction, source access, destination access, or linked-function calls, leaving the bounded poisoned output unchanged.
